messages:
Alex R: heads up — just finished the staged release (v4.2.1). Canary traffic started at ~02:00Z and we're seeing a spike of 5xxs on /v1/generate. PagerDuty just fired.
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident INC-20260315-742 fired (alert: canary-5xx-rate). Notifying on-call.
PagerDuty: New page — canary-5xx-rate — 5xx rate > 5% for 3m on service=runtime-canary. Severity=critical.
Maria G: acked. I'm looking at logs now. Can someone confirm routing? Is this the new tokenizer change? @Alex R
Alex R: ack — rolling release included tokenizer tweak + kernel reprioritization. I saw a small mem bump in canary but expected.
Samir P: looking at canary nodes: 3/5 nodes reporting 502/503s. errors per minute from embed-worker and runtime-proc. grabbing traces.
Maria G: stack traces show NPE in request normalizer during batched decode. snippet: ```java
java.lang.NullPointerException at com.redwood.runtime.RequestNormalizer.normalize(RequestNormalizer.java:142)
```
Maria G: that's the new null-check I added — hmm. 
Alex R: ugh, that was code I pushed earlier today during the last minute fix. OK we should stop the rollout and divert canary traffic back to stable.
Jenna (Ops Lead): propose mitigation: 1) Pause rollout 2) Divert canary traffic to stable 3) Rollback canary release (if pause doesn't stop new instances). Anyone object? :thumbsup: to proceed.
Samir P: running command to pause: `redwood release pause --id v4.2.1 --scope canary` — started.
IncidentBot: release pause acknowledged by orchestration-service. New canary instances will not be created; existing failing instances still serving.
Maria G: divert command executed: `trafficctl set-split runtime 100:0 --target stable,canary` — decreased canary weight to 0%.
PagerDuty: Escalation: second-level on-call alerted due to critical severity and >10min unacknowledged errors.
Alex R: running rollback on canary group: `kubectl -n runtime rollout undo deploy/runtime-canary --to-revision=3` — triggering.
Samir P: rollback in progress. pods terminating, new pods coming up with previous image. watching health checks.
EOps: customer impact check — telemetry shows ~1200 requests failed in last 10m, impacting roughly 0.03% of global requests. Most failures localized to canary region us-west-2. No broad customer reports yet (pager for support quiet).
Maria G: healthchecks are green on restored pods, error rate dropping to <0.2% in canary group after rollback. still some 502 traces from older pods being drained.
Jenna (Ops Lead): good work. We'll keep canary at 0% and hold the release. Alex, Maria — pls open a revert PR for the tokenizer null-check and run unit/regression tests. Samir, keep an eye on the drained pods for 20m.
Alex R: creating revert PR now and kicking off CI. link: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/4123
Samir P: drain done for 5/5 failing pods; error logs tapering.
IncidentBot: Incident INC-20260315-742 updated: mitigation in progress, rollback executed, canary traffic set to 0%.
PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by Maria G at 02:12Z; incident status: acknowledged -> mitigation in progress.
EOps: customer impact note filed: "Canary release v4.2.1 caused localized 5xx spikes in us-west-2 due to a tokenizer null-check regression. Rollback performed; no widespread customer impact detected. 1200 failed requests in 10m window; no SEV1 customer reports."
Jenna (Ops Lead): handing off to night on-call. @Samir P please summarize and pin logs to the incident ticket, then assign to infra-devs for follow-up.
Samir P: summary pinned to INC-20260315-742, logs attached, assigned to @Alex R and @Maria G for fix verification.
Alex R: will run through extra canary tests + add defensive tests for normalizer. ETA for safe re-release: 3-4 hours after tests.
Jenna (Ops Lead): closing loop: if error rate remains <0.1% for 30m with canary at 0%, we'll close alert. Otherwise escalate to full rollback to stable cluster and open bridge.
IncidentBot: Incident INC-20260315-742 status changed to monitoring. Next automated check scheduled in 5m.
Maria G: monitoring looks stable at 02:31Z. I'll keep watch. :white_check_mark:
